Judgment

This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 31.10.2025 passed in Sessions Trial No.192 of 2022 by the learned Special judge, Nikshepakon Ke Hiton Ka Sanrakshan Adhiniyam, 2000, Seoni,
District Seoni (M.P.), whereby the appellants have been convicted under Sections 420/34 and 406/34 of the IPC and Sections 3 and 6 of M.P. Nikshepakon Ke Hiton Ka Sanrakshan Adhiniyam,
2000 and sentenced to undergo seven years R.I. and fine of Rs.10,000/- each, three years R.I. and fine of Rs.1,000/- each, three months R.I. and fine of Rs.1,000/- each and six years R.I. and fine of Rs.50,000/- each respectively, with default stipulations.

sentences.text: The case of the prosecution in brief is that on 09.02.2017, complainant Sunil, Son of Dafelal Thakriya submitted a written complaint at Police Station Kotwali, District Seoni, against the accused persons, who were the Directors and Managers of Arogya Dhan Varsha Developers and Allied Limited, having their office at Zyarat Naka, Seoni (M.P.).

entities.text: Arogya Dhan Varsha Developers and Allied Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It was alleged that NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:63456 2 CRA-10632-2025 the accused induced the general public to invest money in their Company by falsely assuring a return of three times on the deposited amount after a period of six years and three months.

Relying upon such representations, several persons, including the complainant and his family members, deposited substantial amounts i.e. Rs.1,03,000/- by Dafelal Thakriya, Rs.98,300/- by Jethulal Thakriya and Rs.33,000/- by the complainant himself.
After the maturity period elapsed, the investors found the Company office closed and the Directors absconding.
It subsequently came to light that the accused had collected large sums of money from several residents of Seoni and nearby villages and had misappropriated the same.
On the basis of the aforesaid allegations, an FIR was registered at Police Station Kotwali, District Seoni, at Crime No.482 of 2017 for offences punishable under Sections 420 and 406 of the IPC.

The appellants did not examine any witness in their defence.
Upon conclusion of the trial, the appellants were convicted and sentenced as indicated hereinabove.
4. At the outset, learned counsel for the appellants submitted that he does not wish to press the appeal on merits and restricts his submissions only to the question of sentence.

It is submitted that the appellants have already undergone 6 years, 10 months, and 24 days of incarceration, as reflected from the custody report dated 18.11.2025 issued by the Superintendent, Central Jail, Ujjain.
It is urged that they have undergone more than 90% of the substantive sentence.

Considering their conduct in jail and the prolonged custody undergone coupled with the fact that they are first offenders, a prayer is made for reducing the sentence to the period already undergone by the appellants.
5. Learned counsel for the State supported the impugned judgment, but raised no objection to the appeal being considered on the question of sentence alone.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.
